name: erdem-codex-adapter
description: Codex adapter for the Erdem Design System: one skill ($erdem) and an optional small AGENTS.md block. It consumes the canonical protocol and the project-intel engine; it contains neither.

supportedEnvironment.codex: any Codex build that reads skills from .agents/skills and instructions from AGENTS.md as documented by OpenAI
supportedEnvironment.operatingSystems: no platform-specific code; developed and tested on Windows 11 only (macOS and Linux untested)

capabilities: skill: $erdem (design, implementation and mixed tasks, review, context, handoff)
agents-md-block: small managed block in AGENTS.md or AGENTS.override.md (opt-in)
context command: engine status mapped to missing, current, stale, unverifiable, partial, unavailable
handoff drift check: compares a handoff's changed files with the working tree
safe-install: dry run, idempotent, ownership markers, no config.toml or hook changes
notUsed: hooks (documented by OpenAI and present in the CLI, but registration through hooks.json and the trust review could not be verified in the development environment)
config.toml (may contain credentials; never read or written)

user: the marker-delimited block in $CODEX_HOME/AGENTS.md or AGENTS.override.md (opt-in)
project: the marker-delimited block in <project>/AGENTS.md or AGENTS.override.md (opt-in)

compatibilityNotes: Skill location ($HOME/.agents/skills, <repo>/.agents/skills) and AGENTS.md discovery (global then project, 32 KiB default combined limit, one file per directory with AGENTS.override.md taking precedence) are taken from OpenAI's documentation.
Codex detects new skills after a restart.
AGENTS.md is read once per run: a newly installed block applies to the next session.
The skill relies on the agent being able to run `node` in its sandbox; if it cannot, the protocol still works through direct inspection (adapters/GENERIC.md section 9).
